title: Canonical affine-scalar cup, edge and ordinary base-change maps
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be algebraic spaces over a scheme $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with their module direct images and tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Use their fixed small etale models, tensor products and derived categories, and the ringed-site cup products [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product]. Restrict the existing tensor model to flat-term K-flat complexes. For $f:X\to Y$ define the relative derived cup by transposing the tensor of the two counits under $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, using the fixed tensor comparison [def-sfb-space-base-change-comparisons]. Define its ordinary degree-(a,b) module cup by the existing tensor-of-cocycles pairing, then cohomology of this derived map and the augmentation F[0] tensor^L G[0]→(F tensor G)[0], using the classical right-derived comparison. For an affine $Y\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$, use the actual A-linear section functor and scalar restriction from Γ(X,O_X) [def-sfb-space-affine-global-sections]. There is a unique natural scalar comparison between its classical cohomology and the scalar restriction of the recorded global cohomology, normalized on every injective resolution by the cycle inclusion and homology quotient. Define the global element cup through this comparison and the recorded global cup. Tensor of sections is the tensor of their structure-module maps after the inverse left unitor. There is a unique natural Leray edge on all module sheaves, normalized on every injective resolution by the cycle inclusion, the ordinary sections compositor [def-sfb-space-affine-sections-compositors], and the homology quotient. On quasi-coherent coefficients [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] for qcqs f this is exactly the normalized affine higher-image section isomorphism [lem-sfb-space-affine-base-higher-image-sections]. For any morphism g and K in the derived category define the unique map $g^*\mathcal H^q(K)\to\mathcal H^q(Lg^*K)$ characterized on every flat K-flat representative by pulling back its cycle inclusion and descending through its pulled homology quotient, followed by the fixed derived counit. The coefficient augmentation Lg*(F[0])→(g*F)[0] is the existing complex counit and single-complex comparison. For a commuting square $f\circ h=g\circ k$, use the pointwise comparison of the fixed derived pullback compositors [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback]; its counit mate defines exchange Lg*Rf*→Rk*Lh*. Define ordinary $\beta_F^q:g^*R^qf_*F\to R^qk_*h^*F$ by the preceding cocycle map, then cohomology of exchange and of the coefficient augmentation. For $Y\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Y'\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ use the ring map from their actual scheme morphism and [def-sfb-space-affine-hom-comparison]. The ordinary compositor Γ_A h*≅Res Γ_B is uniquely normalized by every compatible chart projection and scalar multiplication. Its derived compositor RΓ_A Rh*≅Res^D RΓ_B is uniquely normalized on every K-injective complex by that ordinary compositor and the actual derived units. Define section pullback by the ordinary adjunction unit followed by this compositor. Define global cohomology pullback by the derived adjunction unit, this derived compositor, and the coefficient augmentation, then cohomology and the exact restriction-of-scalars homology comparison. Use the existing ordinary pullback tensor comparison [def-sfb-space-pullback-tensor-comparison] for all ordinary coefficient tensor identifications. No flatness or finiteness hypothesis is used.
